name: High blood pressure (hypertension)
description: Persistently elevated pressure of blood against artery walls (typically 130/80 mmHg or higher). Often symptomless for years while quietly damaging vessels, the heart, kidneys, and brain.
causes: High salt (sodium) intake and low potassium intake
Excess body weight and physical inactivity
Chronic kidney disease or sleep apnea
harmfulEffects: Stroke and heart attack from damaged, narrowed vessels
Heart enlargement and eventual heart failure
helpfulSupplements: Magnesium (glycinate/citrate) — modest BP reduction in trials
Omega-3 (EPA/DHA) — small systolic reduction
Psyllium husk — indirect support via weight/lipids
sources: NIH ODS — Magnesium and Omega-3 fact sheets
PubMed meta-analyses: beetroot juice and blood pressure (nitric oxide pathway)

name: Atherosclerosis (hardened arteries)
description: Build-up of cholesterol-rich plaque inside artery walls, narrowing them and reducing blood flow. Ruptured plaques cause most heart attacks and strokes.
causes: High LDL cholesterol and low HDL
harmfulEffects: Coronary artery disease and heart attack
helpfulFoods: Extra virgin olive oil — monounsaturated fat + polyphenols
helpfulSupplements: Omega-3 (EPA/DHA) — triglyceride reduction
Psyllium husk — LDL cholesterol reduction
Plant sterols/stanols — block cholesterol absorption
sources: Cochrane reviews — oats/psyllium and LDL cholesterol

name: Coronary heart disease
description: Narrowing of the arteries that feed the heart muscle itself, causing chest pain (angina) or heart attack when blood flow can't meet demand.
causes: High LDL cholesterol, smoking, hypertension, diabetes
Family history of early heart disease
helpfulFoods: Mediterranean-style diet: olive oil, vegetables, fish, legumes
helpfulSupplements: Omega-3 (EPA/DHA)
Plant sterols/stanols
Coenzyme Q10 — discussed with a cardiologist, especially with statins
sources: PREDIMED trial — Mediterranean diet and cardiovascular events (NEJM)

name: Depression
description: A mood disorder with persistent sadness, loss of interest, sleep and appetite changes, and impaired daily functioning. Involves neurotransmitter, inflammatory, and neuroendocrine pathways.
causes: Genetic vulnerability and life stress or trauma
Chronic inflammation and poor gut health (gut-brain axis)
Deficiencies in omega-3, B-vitamins (folate, B12), vitamin D
harmfulEffects: Increased risk of anxiety and substance use
Higher cardiovascular and overall mortality risk
helpfulFoods: Mediterranean-pattern diet — vegetables, legumes, olive oil
helpfulSupplements: Omega-3 high-EPA formulas — best-studied nutritional adjunct
Vitamin D — if deficient
Folate (L-methylfolate) and B12 — if levels are low
S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe) — under professional guidance
sources: SMILES trial — dietary intervention and depression (BMC Medicine)
NIH ODS — Omega-3 and B-vitamin fact sheets

name: Alzheimer's disease
description: Progressive memory and cognitive decline from abnormal protein build-up (amyloid, tau) and neuron loss. The most common cause of dementia.
causes: Untreated hypertension, diabetes, and obesity in mid-life
Poor diet low in antioxidants and omega-3s
harmfulEffects: Loss of independence and self-care ability
helpfulFoods: MIND-diet pattern: leafy greens, berries, nuts
Fatty fish — DHA is a major brain structural fat
helpfulSupplements: Omega-3 DHA — brain structural support
Vitamin D — deficiency linked to faster decline
Vitamin B12 — treat deficiency promptly in older adults
sources: Morris et al., MIND diet and cognitive decline (Alzheimer's & Dementia journal)

name: Migraine
description: Recurrent intense headaches, often one-sided, with nausea and sensitivity to light/sound. Involves abnormal brain excitability and trigeminal nerve inflammation.
causes: Triggers: stress, poor sleep, skipped meals, dehydration
Food triggers in some people: aged cheese, alcohol, MSG
harmfulEffects: Debilitating pain episodes and lost productivity
helpfulFoods: Magnesium-rich foods: leafy greens, nuts, seeds
Regular balanced meals to avoid fasting triggers
helpfulSupplements: Magnesium (400-600 mg/day) — prevention, well-studied
Riboflavin (vitamin B2, 400 mg/day) — preventive trials
Coenzyme Q10 — modest preventive evidence
Feverfew — mixed evidence; discuss with a doctor
sources: Cochrane review — riboflavin for migraine prophylaxis

name: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD)
description: Fat accumulation in liver cells in people who drink little or no alcohol. Ranges from simple fat deposits to inflammation (NASH) and scarring (fibrosis/cirrhosis).
causes: Insulin resistance, obesity, and type 2 diabetes
Rapid weight loss and some medications
harmfulEffects: Liver failure and liver cancer risk
helpfulFoods: Filtered coffee — associated with less liver scarring
Oily fish — omega-3s reduce liver fat in trials
helpfulSupplements: Omega-3 (EPA/DHA) — reduces liver fat in trials
Vitamin E (800 IU) — studied in NASH; use with medical guidance

name: Kidney stones
description: Hard mineral deposits (most often calcium oxalate) that form in the kidneys and cause severe pain when passing through the urinary tract.
causes: Chronic low fluid intake — concentrated urine
High salt and high animal-protein diet
Excess oxalate-rich foods without calcium pairing
Obesity, some metabolic conditions and medications
harmfulEffects: Severe colic pain and urinary blockage
helpfulFoods: Water — 2.5-3 L/day, the single most effective measure
Citrus (lemon, orange) — citrate inhibits stone formation
Calcium-rich foods WITH meals — binds oxalate in the gut
Fruits and vegetables generally — potassium citrate
helpfulSupplements: Potassium citrate — under medical supervision
Magnesium — may reduce oxalate crystallization
sources: American Urological Association — stone prevention guidance

name: Chronic kidney disease (CKD)
description: Gradual, permanent loss of kidney filtering ability, staged 1-5. Usually silent until advanced stages. Dietary management is central and changes as stages progress.
causes: Diabetes and high blood pressure (leading causes)
harmfulEffects: Anemia, bone disease, and cardiovascular strain
End-stage disease requiring dialysis or transplant
helpfulFoods: Stage-dependent — medical dietitian guidance is essential
Cabbage and cruciferous vegetables — lower potassium
helpfulSupplements: Active vitamin D — only as prescribed
Sodium bicarbonate — if prescribed for acid balance
Avoid high-dose vitamin C and herbal supplements in CKD

name: Asthma
description: Chronic airway inflammation causing wheeze, cough, chest tightness, and episodes of breathlessness, often triggered by allergens, exercise, or cold air.
causes: Air pollution, tobacco smoke, and occupational irritants
harmfulEffects: Airway remodeling with poorly controlled disease
Reduced exercise capacity and sleep quality
helpfulFoods: Fruits and vegetables rich in vitamin C — citrus, peppers
Tomatoes — lycopene, associated with less airway reactivity
helpfulSupplements: Vitamin D — supplementation reduced attack rates in deficient patients (Cochrane)
Omega-3 — modest anti-inflammatory support
Magnesium — IV form is used in emergencies; oral role is supportive
sources: Cochrane review — vitamin D and asthma exacerbations
GINA — Global Strategy for Asthma Management

name: COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease)
description: Progressive, largely irreversible airflow limitation (chronic bronchitis + emphysema), most often caused by smoking or long-term pollutant exposure.
causes: Indoor/outdoor air pollution and occupational dusts
harmfulEffects: Weight loss, muscle wasting, heart strain
helpfulFoods: Adequate calories and protein — muscle preservation is critical
Oily fish and anti-inflammatory Mediterranean pattern
Fruit and vegetables — higher intake linked to better lung function
helpfulSupplements: Vitamin D — often low in COPD; deficiency linked to flare-ups
Oral nutritional supplements — when weight loss occurs
Creatine — studied as adjunct in pulmonary rehabilitation
sources: GOLD — Global strategy for COPD (nutrition section)

name: GERD (acid reflux)
description: Backflow of stomach acid into the esophagus causing heartburn, regurgitation, and sometimes cough or voice changes.
causes: Excess weight, large late meals, lying down after eating
Trigger foods: fried, spicy, fatty, chocolate, coffee, alcohol
harmfulEffects: Barrett's esophagus with increased cancer risk if untreated
helpfulSupplements: Alginate-based formulations — form a raft over stomach contents
Deglycyrrhizinated licorice (DGL) — traditional support, limited evidence

name: Peptic ulcer
description: Open sore in the stomach lining (gastric) or first part of the small intestine (duodenal), causing burning upper abdominal pain.
causes: Smoking and alcohol, which impair healing
harmfulEffects: Persistent pain and poor nutrient absorption
helpfulFoods: Fermented foods (yogurt, kimchi, sauerkraut) — studied alongside H. pylori treatment
Broccoli sprouts — sulforaphane studied against H. pylori
Avoid: coffee, alcohol, very spicy foods during flare-ups
helpfulSupplements: Probiotics — improve H. pylori eradication rates alongside antibiotics
Zinc-carnosine — mucosal healing studied in Japan
Deglycyrrhizinated licorice (DGL)
sources: Cochrane review — probiotics and H. pylori eradication

name: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)
description: Chronic abdominal pain with constipation, diarrhea, or both — without structural damage. Gut-brain interaction disorder with microbiome involvement.
causes: Visceral hypersensitivity and altered gut motility
FODMAP food intolerance in many patients
harmfulEffects: Chronic pain, bloating, and unpredictable bowel habits
Anxiety, reduced quality of life, work absenteeism
helpfulFoods: Soluble fiber: oats, psyllium (insoluble bran can worsen symptoms)
helpfulSupplements: Peppermint oil (enteric-coated) — strong trial evidence for IBS pain
Psyllium — evidence-backed soluble fiber
Multi-strain probiotics — strain-specific benefit
sources: American College of Gastroenterology — IBS guidelines

name: Chronic constipation
description: Infrequent (fewer than 3/week) or difficult bowel movements lasting weeks or longer.
causes: Low fiber and low fluid intake
helpfulFoods: Water — fiber needs fluid to work
Kiwi fruit — 2/day improved frequency in trials
helpfulSupplements: Psyllium husk — first-line evidence-backed fiber
Magnesium citrate — draws water into the bowel
Probiotics — B. lactis strains have trial support

name: Type 2 diabetes
description: Chronic elevation of blood glucose from insulin resistance and declining insulin production. Often reversible in early stages with diet, weight loss, and activity.
causes: Excess body fat (especially abdominal) and inactivity
harmfulEffects: Nerve damage (neuropathy), kidney disease, and vision loss
Slow wound healing and foot complications
helpfulFoods: Low-glycemic pattern: beans, lentils, oats, non-starchy vegetables
Fenugreek seeds — improved post-meal glucose in trials
Nuts — reduced HbA1c in trial meta-analyses
Leafy greens — magnesium and low glycemic load
helpfulSupplements: Magnesium — low levels worsen insulin resistance
Cinnamon extract — small HbA1c reduction in meta-analyses
Psyllium — slows glucose absorption with meals
Alpha-lipoic acid — studied for diabetic neuropathy
sources: American Diabetes Association — Standards of Care (lifestyle)
NIH ODS — Cinnamon, Magnesium fact sheets

name: Osteoporosis
description: Progressive loss of bone density and strength, making bones fragile and fracture-prone — most visible in the hip, spine, and wrist after menopause or in older age.
causes: Low lifelong calcium and vitamin D intake
Smoking, excess alcohol, long-term steroid use
harmfulEffects: Fragility fractures — hip fractures carry high mortality in the elderly
Loss of height and stooped posture
helpfulFoods: Leafy greens (kale, bok choy) — absorbable calcium
helpfulSupplements: Calcium (500-600 mg with food) if dietary intake is low
Vitamin D3 — with blood-level monitoring
Vitamin K2 — directs calcium to bone (MK-7 form)
Magnesium — bone matrix cofactor
sources: NIH ODS — Calcium and Vitamin D fact sheets
WHO — Prevention and management of osteoporosis

name: Osteoarthritis
description: Wear-driven degeneration of joint cartilage, causing pain, stiffness, and reduced mobility — typically in knees, hips, and hands.
causes: Excess body weight loading the joints
harmfulEffects: Reduced physical activity → muscle loss and weight gain
helpfulFoods: Oily fish — omega-3s reduce joint inflammation
Extra virgin olive oil — oleocanthal, an NSAID-like compound
Broccoli — sulforaphane studied for cartilage protection
helpfulSupplements: Curcumin — pain reduction comparable to NSAIDs in some trials
Omega-3 (EPA/DHA)
Collagen peptides — joint comfort in trials
Glucosamine/chondroitin — mixed evidence, well tolerated
sources: Osteoarthritis and Cartilage journal — curcumin trials

name: Gout
description: Sudden, severe joint pain (classically the big toe) from uric-acid crystals depositing in joints when blood urate is chronically high.
causes: Diets high in purines: organ meats, some seafood, beer
harmfulEffects: Joint damage and urate crystal tophi
helpfulFoods: Cherries (fresh or juice) — lower gout attack risk in studies
Low-fat dairy — associated with lower urate
Vitamin C-rich fruit — modest urate lowering
Coffee — associated with lower urate levels
Water — plenty; avoid alcohol and sugary drinks
helpfulSupplements: Vitamin C (500 mg/day) — modest urate-lowering in trials
Cherry extract — preliminary evidence
sources: Zhang et al., Cherries and gout attacks (Arthritis & Rheumatism)

name: Acne
description: Inflammation of oil glands and hair follicles producing pimples, blackheads, and cysts — driven by hormones, sebum, bacteria (C. acnes), and inflammation.
causes: High-glycemic diets and dairy (especially skim milk) in susceptible people
helpfulFoods: Low-glycemic whole foods: vegetables, legumes, whole grains
Zinc sources: pumpkin seeds, lentils, cashews
helpfulSupplements: Zinc — anti-inflammatory; studied vs. placebo for acne
Omega-3 — reduced lesion severity in small trials
Probiotics — emerging gut-skin axis evidence
sources: Meta-analyses: low-glycemic diets and acne lesion counts

name: Eczema (atopic dermatitis)
description: Chronic itchy, inflamed, dry skin from a weakened skin barrier and immune over-reactivity — often alongside asthma and allergies.
harmfulEffects: Sleep loss from itch, skin infections
helpfulFoods: Anti-inflammatory pattern: fatty fish, colorful vegetables
Probiotic foods (yogurt, kefir) — early-life studies show prevention benefit
Sunflower seed oil — supports barrier in small studies
helpfulSupplements: Vitamin D — deficiency common in eczema; supplementation helps some
Probiotics (Lactobacillus rhamnosus) — mixed evidence, prevention in infants
Evening primrose/borage oil (GLA) — weak evidence

name: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD)
description: Degeneration of the macula — the central retina responsible for sharp vision — causing a dark or blurred spot in central sight. Leading cause of vision loss over 50.
causes: Low intake of lutein/zeaxanthin and omega-3s
harmfulEffects: Loss of reading and face recognition ability
helpfulFoods: Dark leafy greens: kale, spinach — lutein + zeaxanthin
Oily fish — DHA concentrates in the retina
helpfulSupplements: AREDS2 formula: lutein, zeaxanthin, vitamins C/E, zinc, copper — proven to slow progression
Omega-3 (DHA)

name: Cataracts
description: Clouding of the eye's lens causing gradual blurring, glare, and faded colors — strongly linked to oxidative damage over decades.
harmfulEffects: Eventual blindness if untreated (surgery is curative)
helpfulSupplements: Multivitamin with vitamin C, E, lutein — associated with lower cataract risk in cohorts
Vitamin C — lens concentration depends on diet

name: Dry eye syndrome
description: Insufficient or poor-quality tears causing grittiness, burning, redness, and fatigue — worse with screens, dry air, and contact lenses.
harmfulEffects: Corneal surface damage in severe cases
helpfulFoods: Oily fish — omega-3s improve tear quality
helpfulSupplements: Omega-3 EPA/DHA — improved signs and symptoms in trials (CHED/omega-3 DED studies)
Vitamin A — deficiency causes severe dryness (rare in well-fed populations)
sources: TFOS DEWS II report — Dry Eye Workshop

name: Common cold
description: Viral upper-respiratory infection (mostly rhinoviruses) with runny nose, sore throat, sneezing, and cough — usually resolving within 7-10 days.
causes: Weakened defenses: poor sleep, stress, low vitamin D
helpfulFoods: Chicken soup (homemade) — hydration, mild anti-inflammatory effect
Garlic — allicin; a large trial reduced cold frequency
Ginger and honey — throat soothing (honey not for infants under 1)
Yogurt and fermented foods — microbiome support
helpfulSupplements: Vitamin C — regular use slightly shortens duration
Zinc lozenges — within 24h of onset, may shorten duration
Vitamin D — deficiency correction reduces respiratory infections
Elderberry — modest evidence for symptom relief
sources: Cochrane — Vitamin C and zinc for the common cold
NIH ODS — Vitamin C, Zinc, Vitamin D fact sheets

name: Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid)
description: The thyroid produces too little hormone, slowing metabolism — causing tiredness, weight gain, cold intolerance, dry skin, and low mood.
causes: Thyroid surgery or radioactive iodine treatment
harmfulEffects: Goiter; in pregnancy, risks to fetal brain development
helpfulFoods: Brazil nuts — selenium for T4→T3 conversion
helpfulSupplements: Selenium — 100-200 mcg reduced autoimmune antibody levels in trials
Vitamin D — often low in Hashimoto's
Iodine — only if deficient; excess worsens autoimmune thyroid disease
Note: take levothyroxine 4h apart from calcium/iron supplements
sources: NIH ODS — Iodine, Selenium fact sheets
ATA — American Thyroid Association patient resources
